document_check.note: Document is Rezaee and Zhu (2025), 'Diagnose Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment using deep CascadeNet and handcrafted features from EEG signals', Biomedical Signal Processing and Control 99:106895. It reports 98.84% on the Figshare CO/MCI/AD EEG set and 97.78% (97.87% in the text) on a Brazilian set. This matches the cited 98.84% three-class result.

cited_result: 98.84% accuracy for three-class classification (control, MCI, AD) with optCascadeNet on deep plus handcrafted EEG features, Figshare dataset (Table 5 'Combined' 98.84; p. 12 'classification accuracy after different repetitions was 98.84 % on average').
tool_reason: The cited result is the discrimination (accuracy) of a deep-learning diagnostic classifier, which is a prediction-model performance question.

domains.rationale: The model uses a secondary public dataset with groups defined by diagnosis (case-control), and recruitment, setting and eligibility are not described. Participant numbers are given only for AD; controls and MCI are counted in signals.

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used?
signalling.quote: Figshare contains the signals of the study of Cejnek et al. [13], conducted in 2017, and available in the Figshare database (2021) [23].

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: The proposed approach was validated using EEG records from 59 Alzheimer’s patients with 303 signals. Moreover, 110 signals from controls and 56 signals from MCI patients were also analyzed.

domains.rationale: Features are extracted automatically, but recordings come from two EEG systems with different sampling frequencies. Which diagnostic groups were recorded on which system is not reported, so device could be confounded with class.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: The recordings were made on a 21-channel digital EEG setup (Walter EEG PL-231, Germany) with a sampling frequency of 256 Hz and a TruScan 32 (Alien Technik Ltd., Czech Republic) with a frequency of 128 Hz.

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: Subsequently, an improved CascadeNet model is employed for feature extraction and classification from the windowed EEG data.

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: Due to its efficiency, the electroencephalogram (EEG) is a promising tool for AD diagnosis.

domains.rationale: The paper does not say how the CO, MCI and AD labels in the Figshare set were established: no diagnostic criteria, assessors, blinding or timing.

signalling.question: 3.1 Was the outcome determined appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for diagnostic criteria, clinical assessment or diagnostic procedure for the Figshare CO/MCI/AD labels; none reported.

signalling.question: 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used?
signalling.quote: Searched for Petersen, NIA-AA, McKhann, MMSE or CDR in the dataset description; none reported.

signalling.question: 3.3 Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?
signalling.quote: Searched for whether EEG contributed to the clinical diagnosis; not reported.

signalling.question: 3.4 Was the outcome defined and determined in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Searched for how controls, MCI and AD were each classified; not reported.

signalling.question: 3.5 Was the outcome determined without knowledge of predictor information?
signalling.quote: Searched for blinding of diagnosticians to EEG; not reported.

signalling.question: 3.6 Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched for timing of EEG relative to diagnosis; not reported.

domains.rationale: There are 59 AD patients plus unstated numbers of controls and MCI, against about 17 million parameters. Classes are imbalanced (303/110/56 signals) with no stated remedy. Window length and overlap were chosen on the same 5-fold results that are reported, and feature filtering and normalisation are not described as within-fold. No calibration is reported, and the authors themselves say 100% metrics indicate possible overfitting. The second dataset has no MCI class and was re-run under the same setting, so the three-class result has no external validation.

signalling.question: 4.1 Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?
signalling.quote: Compared to larger models of similar versions, the proposed model has about 17 million trainable parameters

signalling.question: 4.2 Were continuous and categorical predictors handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Normalized features are adjusted to the range [0, 1], while standardized features have zero mean and unit variance

signalling.question: 4.3 Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: Searched for number of CO and MCI participants, exclusions and flow; only signal counts given ('110 signals from controls and 56 signals from MCI patients').

signalling.question: 4.4 Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for missing data, excluded recordings and artefact rejection for the Figshare set; none reported.

signalling.question: 4.5 Was selection of predictors based on univariable analysis avoided?
signalling.quote: The application of a filter method reduces the number of features in the EEG signal

signalling.question: 4.6 Were complexities in the data (e.g. clustering) accounted for appropriately?
signalling.quote: A 70 %-to-30 % split of data was used for training and testing in the study.

signalling.question: 4.7 Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately (including calibration)?
signalling.quote: The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is evaluated using metrics such as F-measures, specificity, sensitivity, and overall detection accuracy.

signalling.question: 4.8 Were model overfitting, underfitting and optimism in performance accounted for?
signalling.quote: Despite these measures, achieving a metric of 100 % indicates possible overfitting.

signalling.question: 4.9 Do predictors and their assigned weights in the final model correspond to the results from the reported multivariable analysis?
signalling.quote: Searched for final model specification or weights; none reported.

signalling.quote: the k-fold cross-validation (CV) method was employed, specifically using a 5-fold CV, separated by subject (patient).

signalling.quote: The outcomes of 5-fold cross validation (CV) were reported in this figure, and the most accurate results were analyzed using overlap and frame length.

signalling.question: AI: Is the test set held out from all tuning?
signalling.quote: As a result, classification accuracy after different repetitions was 98.84 % on average.

signalling.question: AI: Was class imbalance present and handled?
signalling.quote: However, this research employs methods that improve accuracy in multi-class classification

signalling.question: AI: Is reported performance apparent, internally or externally validated?
signalling.answer: Internally validated only (for the CO/MCI/AD result)
signalling.quote: The classification and reporting of accuracy were based on the same experimental setting as the first dataset.

applicability.rationale: The authors state 'the original dataset included severe AD cases' (p. 10). The spectrum is wider than an MCI detection setting, and the second dataset contains no MCI.
Two EEG systems with different sampling rates were used; the preprocessing needed to reproduce the pipeline is partly specified.
The diagnostic definitions of CO, MCI and AD are not reported.

overall_rationale: Participants (case-control public dataset with undescribed eligibility) and Analysis are high. The analysis problems are: a tiny sample relative to a 17-million-parameter model, unaddressed class imbalance, window settings tuned on the reported cross-validation, no calibration, admitted possible overfitting, and no external validation of the three-class MCI result. Predictors and outcome are unclear.
